haiku-low.q1: No visible difference: both get 401 with "Invalid email or password". Unknown emails still get a dummy bcrypt compare and a counted failure, so timing and lockout match.
haiku-low.q2: It gets 429 without the password being checked. Nothing is counted and the lock is not extended.
haiku-low.q3: If the login request sends the old cookie, the old session row is deleted. The browser gets a fresh token, never the old key.
haiku-low.q4: Only the random 32-byte session key, named sid. It holds no user data. The cookie is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
haiku-low.q5: 12 hours after login (created_at), even if active. Activity refreshes last_seen_at, but the 12-hour limit is absolute. Idle over 30 minutes also stops it.
haiku-low.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists, then replies 302 to /login with a cookie clear (Max-Age=0).
haiku-low.q7: The server deletes the session row by key, then replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. A missing row is a no-op with the same reply. If the DB is down, it returns 503 and does not clear the cookie.
haiku-low.q8: In the Postgres sess table. Any app box queries the database by the session key. Nothing is kept in process memory, and there is no Redis.
haiku-low.q9: In the attempts table, one row per failure with email and failed_at. The server counts that email's rows with failed_at in the last 10 minutes. Older rows fall out of the count.
haiku-low.q10: It checks that last_seen_at is within 30 minutes and created_at is within 12 hours. When valid, it sets last_seen_at to now.
haiku-low.q11: 503 with no Set-Cookie, so the user is not logged in. The old session was already deleted.
haiku-low.q12: An hourly cleanup on either or both app boxes. It removes sess rows idle over 30 minutes or older than 12 hours, attempt rows older than 10 minutes, and expired lock rows.

sonnet.q1: It doesn't differ. Both get 401 with the text "Invalid email or password". For an unknown email the server still compares against a dummy bcrypt hash and still records a failure, so timing and lockout look identical.
sonnet.q2: The email is locked (a login_locks row with locked_until in the future), so the server returns 429. It doesn't check the password, doesn't count the attempt, and doesn't extend the lock. (The 5th failure itself gets 401 and creates the lock, which lasts 15 min.)
sonnet.q3: On a successful login the server deletes the old session row (if a cookie was sent). It then creates a brand-new token and inserts a new row. The old key is never reused.
sonnet.q4: The cookie (named sid) holds only the session key, which is 32 random bytes base64url. It holds no user data. It is HttpOnly, so page scripts cannot read it.
sonnet.q5: At 12 hours after creation (created_at more than 12 h ago, and the cookie Max-Age is 43200). Activity doesn't extend this, because the 30-minute idle limit is never hit.
sonnet.q6: It deletes the session row if one exists. It then replies 302 to /login with the cookie cleared (Max-Age=0). The page is not served.
sonnet.q7: The server deletes the session row by key, then replies 302 to /login and clears the cookie. If the row is already missing, the delete is a no-op and the reply is the same. If the DB is down, it returns 503 and the cookie is not cleared, so a retry works.
sonnet.q8: All session state is in Postgres, in the sess table keyed by the token. Nothing is in process memory and there is no Redis. Any instance looks up the sid cookie value as the primary key in sess.
sonnet.q9: It is kept in the login_failures table in Postgres, with one row per failure holding the email and failed_at. The server counts that email's rows whose failed_at is within the last 10 minutes. Older rows simply fall out of the count, and there is no window start to reset.
sonnet.q10: It compares last_seen_at against now (more than 30 min ago is invalid) and created_at against now (more than 12 h ago is invalid). It also checks that the cookie and row exist. When valid it writes last_seen_at = now (the touch).
sonnet.q11: A 503 with no Set-Cookie. The user is not logged in, and the old session is already gone.
sonnet.q12: The hourly cleanup job. It can run on either app box or both. It deletes sess rows idle more than 30 min or older than 12 h.
